text:
A fresh government audit indicates that the "Obamaphone" initiative has accumulated approximately $9 billion in private financial institutions rather than depositing the funds into the federal treasury, according to recent findings that highlight substantial financial windfalls for telecommunications providers. 

The widely discussed Lifeline Program, which supplies cellular devices to low-income individuals, has drawn scrutiny after a Government Accountability Office (GAO) evaluation suggested that over a third of participants might not meet eligibility requirements. Originally established prior to the Obama administration, the cellphone distribution effort became a prominent emblem of governmental inefficiency during that era, earning widespread notoriety alongside viral moments like that of the Cleveland resident who expressed support on camera for the program before later appearing in a follow-up interview to voice disillusionment with the administration.

According to a 90-page analysis requested by Missouri Democratic Senator Claire McCaskill, who serves as the ranking member on the Senate's principal oversight committee and previously worked as a state auditor, the initiative is failing the public due to absent supervision. Describing the current system as reliant on an honor code that permits telecommunications firms to regularly collect government disbursements without adequate checks, McCaskill emphasized that the setup is unsustainable.

Reporting by The Daily Caller noted that the extensive 90-page GAO document points to widespread dishonesty on application forms, with undercover tests revealing that ineligible submissions gained approval in 63 percent of cases. Furthermore, audits indicated that between 36 and 65 percent of recipients across different categories provided easily disprovable false information yet still received benefits. 

This high level of deception occurred largely because the Federal Communications Commission delegated screening duties to telecommunications businesses that stand to gain financially from maximizing their enrollment numbers. During GAO undercover tests, investigators submitted 19 applications using deliberately flawed criteria and successfully secured Lifeline services from 12 out of 19 providers by utilizing fabricated eligibility papers. Applicants merely needed to claim participation in alternative assistance initiatives such as food stamps or supplemental security income.

When legislative changes were previously debated, telecommunications enterprises placed daily full-page advertisements in outlets circulated among Capitol Hill employees. Notably, the spouse of the chief executive officer for TracFone, the primary recipient of the program's funds, served as a major political fundraiser for former President Barack Obama.

The drivers behind these unprecedented fraud levels stemmed from the FCC permitting entities with financial incentives to handle enrollment verification. Providers frequently parked neon-lit vans outside public housing complexes and welfare offices to sign up customers; one woman recounted to The Daily Caller News Foundation Investigative Group that a representative outside an assistance office urged her to register her toddler. 

Investigators discovered that firms neglected to verify qualifications while the FCC failed to enforce compliance or penalize violators. Furthermore, the agency did not supply numerous providers with access to inter-agency databases that could have facilitated basic verification procedures. 

Meanwhile, Michelle Dowry, frequently referred to as the "Obamaphone Lady," subsequently appeared on the program hosted by Alex Jones to state she had become disillusioned, concluding that the administration's promises amounted to a hoax and that the primary tangible offering received by minority communities during the eight-year period was a publicly funded mobile device.

Both he and his senior advisors maintain the perspective that Democrats are attempting to undermine the legitimacy of his November 8 electoral win by claiming that Moscow intervened to assist his campaign.

Meanwhile, U.S. intelligence leaders have maintained a high level of certainty that the Russian government orchestrated the cyber attacks against political targets in a bid to aid Trump's presidential run. In response to these cyber operations, President Barack Obama took action the previous week by ordering the expulsion of thirty-five Russian intelligence operatives from the United States alongside the closure of two Russian diplomatic compounds. 

Speaking with journalists on Saturday at his resort located in Palm Beach, Florida, Trump asserted that he possessed inside information regarding the breaches that others were unaware of, concluding that certainty about the culprit was impossible. BAGHDAD (Reuters) - Baghdad declared on Thursday that negotiations regarding the reopening of airports and the supply of foreign currency to banks in the Kurdish autonomous zone will remain off the table unless the regional authorities pledge to uphold the unity of Iraq. Following a September 25 independence vote that the central government deemed unlawful, international flights into the territory were grounded. Furthermore, authorities in Baghdad have urged neighboring nations to close off the borders of the landlocked area. Additional isolation tactics included halting dollar sales to four banks owned by Kurds and demanding an end to independent petroleum exports. 

Despite the overwhelming vote in favor of secession, Kurdish leaders have repeatedly pushed for talks. In an official release, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) urged Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi to engage in dialogue based on the Iraqi Constitution in order to bypass what they termed collective punishment. The KRG expressed readiness for discussions concerning border crossings, commercial trade, public services, banking institutions, and aviation hubs. 

Nonetheless, a spokesperson for the Iraqi administration stated that any dialogue is contingent upon the Kurds renouncing the outcome of the referendum and committing fully to a unified nation. Speaking to Reuters, the official emphasized that the KRG has to recognize federal sovereignty regarding border security, air and land entry points, safety, and petroleum shipments. 

Generations of Kurds have pursued statehood, arguing that the September referendum was merely intended to initiate peaceful negotiations for eventual independence alongside Baghdad. However, the federal government rejected the vote entirely, pointing out that it took place not only within the autonomous zone but also across contested neighboring territories controlled by Kurdish fighters. 

Neighboring Turkey and Iran, both fierce opponents of Kurdish separatism, have backed Baghdad's rigid stance. Even Washington, a long-time ally of the Kurds, had urged them to call off the vote beforehand. On Thursday, an official speaking for Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan announced that Turkey plans to phase out operations at border crossings with the northern region, working alongside the governments in Baghdad and Iran. Additionally, Turkish Prime Minister Binali Yildirim is scheduled to travel to Baghdad on Sunday for discussions with Haidar Abadi.

Friction escalated Wednesday when Kurdish officials alleged that Iraqi troops and Iranian-backed paramilitaries were massing for a significant offensive against Kirkuk—an oil-rich zone—and territory near Mosul. Both areas lie outside the official autonomous region but have been secured by Kurdish forces since the expulsion of Islamic State militants. 

Baghdad rejected claims of an impending military campaign. Prime Minister Abadi assured the public in a written statement that military forces would not be deployed against Kurdish citizens or used to instigate war. A military representative reiterated that no offensive against Kurdish units was underway, explaining instead that government forces were positioning themselves to clear Islamic State fighters from territory near the Syrian border. 

In a related legal development, Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council ordered the arrest on Wednesday of the Kurdish referendum commission's chairman and two assistants for defying an existing court order that had declared the independence vote unconstitutional.

Kirkuk, a ethnically diverse province boasting substantial oil deposits and currently secured by Kurdish fighters, has become a central flashpoint due to competing claims from both the central government and the KRG. Shiite Muslim paramilitaries, known as Popular Mobilisation, alongside federal troops, have taken positions to the south and west of the city in sectors previously held by Islamic State. The Iraqi government spokesperson noted that recognizing federal authority over Kirkuk is yet another prerequisite for any future negotiations.

Meanwhile, Islamic State remnants continue to hold ground near al-Qaim, where the Euphrates river flows from Syria into Iraq. This marks the final pocket of the country still controlled by the militant group, which seized a third of Iraqi territory back in 2014. On Thursday, the military targeted al-Qaim by dropping leaflets instructing insurgents to surrender or face execution. 

While IS still maintains pockets across the border in Syria, it is currently retreating under pressure from multiple opposing forces, including a U.S.-backed and Kurdish-led coalition, as well as Syrian government troops supported by foreign Shiite militias tied to Iran and Russia. The cross-border militant caliphate effectively shattered in July when U.S.-supported Iraqi forces reclaimed Mosul—the group's primary stronghold in Iraq—following a protracted nine-month campaign.

text:
SAN JUAN, PUERTO RICO — Medical infrastructure across Puerto Rico has plunged into a severe crisis following Hurricane Maria. As the most powerful storm to impact the territory in decades, it left healthcare facilities flooded, covered in debris, and heavily reliant on diesel generators to keep vulnerable patients alive. This precarious condition deepens the suffering across the U.S. territory, home to 3.4 million American citizens. 

For certain individuals, evacuation to the United States remains the sole viable path for medical care. Cheira Ruiz and her infant daughter, Gabriellyz—born two weeks ago with a complex heart defect—faced precisely this situation. The newborn was admitted to the Centro Cardiovascular de Puerto Rico in the capital just before Maria struck the previous Wednesday, though operating under such conditions proved impossible for the medical staff. 

Gabriellyz qualified as one of the earliest infants cleared for an emergency medical flight departing the island post-storm. Living two hours south of San Juan in Guanica, her parents received the positive news on Friday when emergency personnel visited their residence to advise them to prepare for a journey to Miami. Because telephone lines were down, physicians had contacted a local radio station to broadcast an appeal for help finding the family. Prior to departure, however, the parents were informed that space permitted only one accompanying passenger, leaving the mother and child to fly to Miami alone. Ruiz expressed her emotional strain on Saturday, noting she was trying to maintain her strength.

Residents across the island awoke to a drastically altered environment after the disaster. Food supplies are running low, and the collapsed electrical grid could take months to repair. Long lines of pedestrians and motorists stretch for blocks as people attempt to secure limited fuel for vehicles and backup generators. With cellular networks, the internet, and email virtually non-existent, the modern infrastructure has been thrust backward in time, leaving radio as a primary lifeline for news.

Hospitals face mounting hurdles everywhere. Backup generators failed rapidly at certain facilities after the power cut out, while others are exhausting their diesel reserves. Fuel has become so scarce that armed escorts now deliver it to prevent theft, according to Dr. Ivan Gonzalez Cancel, who serves as a cardiovascular surgeon and heads the heart transplant program at the Centro Cardiovascular. Gonzalez Cancel mentioned that another facility requested the transfer of two critical patients due to a lack of power, a request they had to decline because they faced identical conditions.

Healthcare workers are similarly struggling with gasoline shortages for their daily commutes, with individuals waiting as long as seven hours at the few operational gas stations. Marilyn Rivera Morales, a nurse at the facility, noted she possessed just enough fuel to drive to work for another two days. Gonzalez Cancel questioned how staff members would manage to arrive if gas supplies ran out entirely.

The fuel shortage represents only the beginning of the center's troubles. Describing the cardiovascular facility as being in shambles, Gonzalez Cancel pointed out that operating room walls dripped with condensation and floors remained slick due to the absence of air conditioning. Although most patients had been discharged or sent elsewhere, a number remained because their relatives could not be reached via telephone. 

Outside the cardiac center on Saturday, Savannah, Georgia residents Jorge Rivera and his wife Dorca spoke with Gonzalez Cancel regarding her father, who was still inside awaiting a triple-bypass operation. The couple had been visiting the island to look after their family member. With operations scaling back and the local infrastructure crippled, Gonzalez Cancel calculated that open-heart procedures would be suspended for a month or longer, advising the couple to leave. Stressing that he spoke not just as a physician but as a human being, he urged them to secure a flight to Miami, noting the trip takes only two and a half hours.

Departure, however, remains complicated. With the main airport still hobbled, Gonzalez Cancel explained that securing a special waiver from officials was necessary to obtain the medical evacuation flight for baby Gabriellyz. On Sunday, airport travelers without existing tickets were informed that outbound flights might not be available until October 4. 

Officials anticipate that conditions within local hospitals could deteriorate further before any recovery begins. At the territory's largest public hospital, Centro Medico, a disaster medical assistance team deployed by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is currently establishing makeshift medical units. Commander Michael Garner, a regional coordinator for the operation, suggested this might represent a temporary lull prior to a surge of admissions as other facilities exhaust their generators. 

Garner noted that while the destruction matches that seen during hurricanes Katrina, Harvey, and Irma, Puerto Rico's isolation, communication breakdowns, and fragile infrastructure magnify logistical recovery hurdles substantially. U.S. Air Force Colonel Michael Valle, who arrived on Friday to assist, concurred, emphasizing that the situation feels considerably worse because incoming resources must arrive entirely by air or sea rather than by driving across state lines.

Complicating matters further, a dam in Puerto Rico compromised by heavy rains faced a potential failure on Sunday, threatening communities along the rising Guajataca River. The National Weather Service issued a warning that potential flooding would pose a life-threatening hazard, advising individuals to stay away or risk being swept away.

With the humanitarian crisis expanding, the death toll in Puerto Rico has reached at least 10. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has shared social media imagery showing federal personnel deployed locally, including Coast Guard and search-and-rescue units. Nonetheless, public frustration regarding the pace of aid is growing. Gonzalez Cancel called for a massive military response, while Rivera—a 49-year-old Iraq War veteran waiting for news of his father-in-law—remarked that military assistance has operational limits and predicted the island will require months to recover. He stated that divine intervention feels nearly necessary to fix every light bulb. Dr. Juan Carlos Sotomonte, medical director for Centro Medico’s cardiovascular unit, emphasized that prompt action, divine or otherwise, is urgently required to prevent fatalities from escalating.

Trump’s Health and Human Services secretary, Tom Price, recently made the controversial argument that insurance companies ought to have the permission to charge older and ill individuals higher rates. Discussions surrounding healthcare have produced various harsh statements from conservatives, yet this position certainly stands out. 

Price contended that unless insurers are permitted to levy steep costs on sicker and older populations—to the point where coverage becomes unaffordable—the market will be left with zero insurance providers altogether. Highlighting the stance of remaining insurers, he pointed out their warnings that without market stabilization and the ability to price according to individual risk, they will be forced to withdraw completely. His proposed remedy for this situation is permitting providers to set prices so high that sick individuals are effectively priced out of obtaining coverage entirely. 

This raises a fundamental question: what is the actual purpose of carrying insurance if it vanishes precisely when it is needed most? Isn't the entire point of insurance to assist with skyrocketing medical expenses during times of illness? Pursuing a policy where individuals are left unable to afford doctors, treatments, and medications simply to protect insurance company profits is deeply unsettling. Access to healthcare is widely regarded as a fundamental human right rather than merely a privilege for the wealthy. 

An excerpt capturing Trump’s health and human services secretary supporting higher costs for sick individuals can be viewed via a video clip shared online by CAP Action in March 2017.

Pirro responded with a sarcastic retort of her own, telling Al that if suspects were imprisoned, President Obama would simply release them. 

Nonetheless, certain members of the Fox News audience voiced a commitment to constitutional law, order, and the necessity of thoroughly investigating suspects instead of executing individuals arbitrarily. A viewer named Kimberly pushed back against the sentiment, advising others not to get ahead of themselves because everyone is entitled to a fair trial and the courts should make the final decision. This pushback provoked a furious reaction from Pirro, who mocked Kimberly on air. Snorting in response, Pirro boasted that she had frequently drafted legislation to lengthen criminal sentences and that the judiciary's role is merely to enforce the laws created by lawmakers.

Members of the United States Senate have had enough of Donald Trump's behavior regarding white supremacists and are moving to compel him to enter a formal, legal condemnation on the record.

A few weeks prior, the country and the world observed in dismay as Ku Klux Klan members, neo-Nazis, white supremacists, and other white power factions gathered in Charlottesville, Virginia. The hostile demonstrations ultimately led to the death of Heather Heyer, a 32-year-old counter-protester. 

The situation grew even more tense due to Donald Trump's initial reaction to the violence. Rather than immediately denouncing white supremacy, Trump drew a parallel between the white supremacists and the individuals protesting against them, only naming and condemning the hate groups later when pressure mounted. Shortly after, during a lengthy press conference, Trump reverted to claiming the opposing side was equally culpable. 

According to Politico, a bipartisan coalition of Senators—comprising Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Warner (D-VA), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), and Cory Gardner (R-CO)—has introduced a resolution requiring Trump to issue a legal statement addressing the events in Charlottesville. Furthermore, the measure compels Trump to officially and permanently commit to rejecting neo-Nazis, white nationalists, white supremacists, the Ku Klux Klan, and additional hate groups. 

While typical resolutions tend to be non-controversial and merely symbolic—often honoring notable individuals or designating honorary holidays—this initiative, known as the Charlottesville Resolution, aims to definitively address Trump's perceived leniency toward these organizations. 

Senator Mark Warner issued a statement emphasizing that the events in Charlottesville constituted an act of domestic terrorism committed by a white supremacist, which resulted in the death of Heather Heyer while she opposed bigotry. He added that lawmakers would urge their colleagues to pass the resolution swiftly and unanimously to demonstrate that Congress rejects racist violence and rhetoric unconditionally.

Senator Tim Kaine also released a statement noting that the violent demonstrations in Charlottesville resulted in the loss of three Virginians: Heather Heyer, along with Virginia State Police officers Lieutenant Jay Cullen and Trooper Pilot Berke Bates. Kaine stated that the resolution pays tribute to their lives, supports the healing process in Charlottesville, and urges everyone—including President Trump—to improve efforts in fighting hatred.

Lawmakers will find themselves compelled to support the measure to avoid being associated with Nazi sympathy politically. Unlike Trump, other politicians lack a devoted following that would shield them from the consequences of opposing the resolution. Consequently, Trump faces the prospect of signing the Charlottesville Resolution, securing its place in presidential records indefinitely.

MOSCOW (Reuters) — In a move that could indicate anticipation of fresh American penalties, Moscow has introduced a legislative proposal to conceal the identities of financial institutions that provide funding to state-owned weapons manufacturers. Should the measure pass, the central bank would be relieved of its current obligation to disclose the roster of lenders involved in the defense sector, a group that stood at eight institutions at the beginning of October. 

Furthermore, the legislation would grant both the presidency and the government the authority to designate any bank of their choosing for these defense transactions while eliminating the requirement to make the selection criteria public. Present rules stipulate that only lenders controlled by the state or the central bank possessing capital of at least 100 billion rubles, equivalent to $1.7 billion, are eligible for such agreements. 

The legislative push comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin convened a session on Tuesday focused on strengthening the nation's armed forces. 

Relations have remained tense following an August sanctions package signed by U.S. President Donald Trump, intended to penalize Moscow following U.S. intelligence findings of interference in the 2016 American presidential election—claims that the Kremlin has consistently rejected. In connection with that legislation, the U.S. State Department released a roster of 39 Russian intelligence and defense entities last month.

The American legislation mandates that the U.S. president penalize any individual determined to have participated in a substantial transaction with entities operating within or on behalf of Russia's defense or intelligence apparatus. Although this step does not instantly enact fresh sanctions, administration officials noted in October that decisions will be evaluated individually.

Institutions currently appearing on the public disclosure list feature major state-run entities such as Sberbank, VTB, and the Russian Agriculture Bank, alongside privately owned Rossiya and Gazprombank, the latter of which counts the gas giant Gazprom among its stakeholders. 

Meanwhile, three insiders familiar with the discussions revealed to Reuters that Sberbank has suggested creating a dedicated financial institution specifically for backing the country's military sector as a strategy to evade restrictions. Sberbank chose not to issue a statement regarding the matter.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) — A faction of 20 moderate House Republicans cautioned on Friday that the push to revise the federal tax code faces serious threats if the upcoming fiscal 2018 budget resolution insists on deep spending reductions. 

Representing the moderate Tuesday Group, these lawmakers addressed a June 30 letter to House Speaker Paul Ryan. They argued that mandating hundreds of billions in cuts to mandatory programs would create severe obstacles for tax reform. Consequently, they urged that the budget process be postponed until Senate Republicans conclude their deliberations on healthcare. 

Spearheaded by Pennsylvania Representative Charlie Dent, the group stated that continuing down the current legislative path threatens to derail tax overhaul efforts. Securing a 2018 budget resolution is mandatory for Republicans to utilize reconciliation, a procedural mechanism that allows a tax package to advance without Democratic votes. 

However, hardline conservatives in the House Freedom Caucus are conditioning their support for any fiscal blueprint on substantial rollbacks to mandatory programs, specifically targeting Medicaid and food stamps—reductions that the moderate faction firmly rejects. 

AshLee Strong, a spokeswoman for Ryan, noted in a released statement that the party has advanced considerably regarding budget choices, and these internal discussions will persist among the conference. Both the Freedom Caucus and the Tuesday Group hold enough voting strength individually to block legislation in the House. 

The brewing conflict has also alarmed external entities, particularly influential business lobbies who fear a political impasse might ultimately kill tax reform entirely. 

On Wednesday, a coalition consisting of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the Business Roundtable, the National Association of Manufacturers, and the National Federation of Independent Business issued a joint correspondence to congressional leaders from both parties, emphasizing that comprehensive, pro-growth tax reform remains the paramount reform under consideration. 

Furthermore, congressional aides noted that moderate Republicans are concerned that incorporating mandatory spending cuts into a reconciliation bill would produce politically toxic legislation, slashing assistance for low-income populations while simultaneously delivering tax relief to corporations and high-earning individuals. 

Amid these divisions, the House Budget Committee scrapped its schedule to bring the fiscal 2018 resolution to the floor this week. The decision followed pushback from several committee chairmen who resisted directives to extract $250 billion in mandatory spending, an amount that still falls well short of the far deeper cuts demanded by Freedom Caucus members.

While moderate Republicans have pressured the president to dismiss Bannon, Trump refrained from offering a public endorsement during a press conference at Trump Tower in New York on Tuesday, though he left the door open regarding the strategist's future, telling reporters that they would see what happens with Mr. Bannon.

During a Sunday television appearance, McMaster repeatedly sidestepped questions regarding his ability to collaborate with Bannon. Neither Bannon nor McMaster provided comments when contacted. 

Aside from termination, options available to Trump include reassigning McMaster outside the White House—potentially returning him to an active military command—or enforcing a truce while keeping both officials in their current roles. Bannon has previously navigated internal power struggles, eventually reaching a detente with the president's son-in-law and senior adviser, Jared Kushner, following a reprimand from Trump. 

Sources supporting McMaster indicated that Chief of Staff Kelly is displeased that the anti-McMaster campaign is projecting an image of internal disarray, complicating his efforts to bring order and discipline to the administration just two weeks into his tenure. Ideologically, Bannon views himself as a champion of Trump's nationalist agenda, advocating for the termination or renegotiation of trade agreements and a more isolationist foreign policy compared to McMaster. Bannon has pushed to abandon the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, which McMaster supports maintaining, and has suggested utilizing private contractors for the conflict in Afghanistan rather than increasing U.S. troop levels, a move advocated by the national security adviser. 

McMaster belongs to a more pragmatic faction that Bannon's camp frequently labels as "globalists." Tensions flared when McMaster restructured the National Security Council, removing four staffers considered close to Bannon. 

Mike Cernovich, a conservative commentator and Bannon supporter, has emerged as a vocal critic of McMaster, launching personal attacks against him. While stating he does not communicate directly with Bannon, Cernovich regards him as a vital counterweight to McMaster and cautions that dismissing Bannon would alienate the president's most dedicated base, suggesting supporters would question the value of backing the administration rather than actively fighting it. 

Additionally, the Zionist Organization of America (ZOA), a conservative Jewish-American and pro-Israel organization with ties to Bannon, has emerged as one of McMaster's fiercest detractors, pushing Trump to remove McMaster from portfolios involving Israel and Iran. Trump himself has defended McMaster, describing him as a good man who is strongly pro-Israel. 

An individual connected to the ZOA rejected the notion that Bannon dictates the group's stance, asserting that they would not abandon their campaign against McMaster despite reportedly receiving requests from Bannon to tone it down. The source expressed deep offense at the suggestion that outside figures direct their messaging, adding that it felt unfortunate to see Bannon taking the blame for actions they insisted were entirely independent.

text:
Have you heard us yet, NFL? Monday Night Football audience numbers are in a tailspin.

The National Football League has transformed into a platform for an anti-law enforcement agenda promoted by Barack Obama, Eric Holder, Al Sharpton, and currently, Black Lives Matter activist Colin Kaepernick along with other football players. It began when Beyoncé delivered a Black Panther, anti-police routine during the Super Bowl in 2016, and the league offered no response. Following that, Isaiah Crowell of the Cleveland Browns shared an image on Instagram resembling ISIS content, featuring a masked individual cutting a police officer's throat, while the league remained quiet. When the Dallas Cowboys sought to display a commemorative sticker honoring five police officers killed in their city by a Black Lives Matter sympathizer during a warmup, the organization denied the request. Meanwhile, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick decided that remaining seated during the national anthem would effectively express his contempt for law enforcement, and the league chose not to comment. It appeared the organization had no issue with disrespecting the flag.

As time went on, additional players participated in Kaepernick's anti-American protests. Eventually, amateur athletes in high schools and colleges, motivated by the media coverage surrounding Kaepernick's actions, began copying the behavior. Certain individuals took a knee during the anthem and staged die-in demonstrations for heightened dramatic impact, each act showing disrespect to the national flag.

The response from the league was nonexistent.

The moment has arrived for the public to demonstrate its opinion regarding this lack of action. Devoted football enthusiasts are staging a quiet boycott by turning off their television sets, a measure bound to impact an enterprise that depends entirely on audience engagement.

Up to this point, the public's pushback against the league appears to be having an effect.

It is probable that the online #BoycottNFL movements and public anger over player demonstrations during the anthem have negatively impacted audience numbers during the current campaign. Furthermore, the shift away from traditional cable packages continues to impact standard television viewership significantly. Yet, might there be additional factors involved?

Only a short time has passed since the league broke audience records across the board, but the organization is currently heading toward its worst viewership figures in a long time, representing a swift and unexpected reversal.

Considering the politically charged disputes and the numerous alternative viewing platforms available currently, has a tipping point of exhaustion with the sport been reached? The statistics point to that conclusion.

The recent Monday Night Football game featuring the Minnesota Vikings against the New York Giants secured a 9.1 overnight audience metric, representing an eight percent decline compared to the matching Week 4 fixture from the previous year featuring the Detroit Lions and the Seattle Seahawks. Furthermore, the 2014 matchup between the New England Patriots and the Kansas City Chiefs achieved a 9.6 metric, according to Forbes.

text:
During a Delta flight departing from Detroit, a man nearly died after a flight attendant failed to believe that a Black woman could work as a medical doctor. Despite living in 2016, the airline employee apparently doubted that individuals with dark skin are permitted to hold such positions. The crew of Delta flight DL945 faced an emergency when a passenger lost consciousness, prompting them to search for medical assistance. Dr. Tamika Cross attempted to step in, but the crew did not believe someone of her complexion could be a medical professional. Cross shared her experience and frustration in a Facebook post directed at the airline.

When the crew asked for help and Cross raised her hand to identify herself as a physician, a flight attendant dismissed her, telling her to put her hand down because they needed actual physicians, nurses, or other medical personnel, and had no time to talk to her while someone was dying. Even as Cross tried to explain her credentials, the employee spoke over her with condescension. As no other medical personnel responded, the crew continued to ask for any physician on board to press their call button. When Cross pressed hers, the same crew member expressed shock that she was an actual physician, demanded to see her credentials, and interrogated her with questions about her specialty, her workplace, and her reason for being in Detroit, all while a man was dying.

Ultimately, a white man stepped forward, and the crew accepted his help, telling Cross that they had found someone who could assist and that he had his credentials, though Cross noted that he never actually showed them anything. Following the incident, the same flight crew member approached Cross to ask about treatment methods before offering an apology for the biased behavior and attempting to compensate her with SkyMiles, which Cross declined.

text:
BEIJING (Reuters) - Following widespread outrage over suspected child abuse at a private Beijing preschool, Beijing announced plans on Thursday to implement stricter monitoring of kindergarten educators, which will involve more thorough verification of their credentials. This incident has acted as a catalyst for public frustration regarding inadequate regulation, meager salaries, and a shortage of qualified staff within the country's rapidly expanding private preschool industry. Public fury surged on social media last week following accusations that children had been mistreated by staff at a Beijing facility operated by the New York-listed company RYB Education. However, local law enforcement stated on Tuesday that specific allegations—including claims that minors were administered pills or stripped by medical personnel for examinations—were baseless.

Deputy Education Minister Tian Xuejun, responding to an inquiry from Reuters regarding the controversy, stated that the ministry intends to enhance background checks for prospective educators and implement more stringent supervision protocols. While noting that the vast majority of instructors are diligent professionals dedicated to creating joyful spaces for children, Tian acknowledged that regrettable isolated events have indeed occurred. He linked these occurrences to a shortfall in top-tier preschool options relative to parental demand, suggesting that such kindergarten incidents highlight a disparity between the public's strong need for preschool facilities and the uneven, insufficient progress of the educational sector.

Tian's perspective aligned with remarks made by President Xi Jinping during a major Communist Party assembly in October, where Xi identified the primary challenge in Chinese society as an unbalanced and unequal level of development that falls short of fulfilling the populace's aspirations for a better standard of living. Meanwhile, specialists observed that RYB seems to have navigated the crisis successfully, with company shares rebounding from initial post-scandal drops, aided by the founder's prompt and proficient crisis response. Nevertheless, educators and researchers emphasize that eliminating maltreatment continues to be a difficult task nationwide, particularly within private, franchised institutions where admission rivalry is intense and staff regulations tend to be laxer.

text: During a Saturday appearance in Chicago, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren addressed the ongoing debate surrounding the repeal of Obamacare by ridiculing Republican efforts to present a viable alternative to the government-regulated healthcare system she previously supported. While speaking to the audience, the potential 2020 Democratic presidential hopeful remarked that she hoped conservatives would leave their remains to science so that she could personally cut them open. Warren questioned what planet her political opponents inhabit before reiterating her desire to perform the procedure on their deceased bodies. This rhetoric aligns with a broader pattern among Democrats of utilizing inflammatory language against political adversaries while simultaneously accusing the opposition of intolerance. Critics frequently recall controversies surrounding Warren's past academic applications regarding her claimed Cherokee and Delaware ancestry as her political profile continues to rise.

text:
Trump Is So Obsessed He Even Has Obama’s Name Coded Into His Website (IMAGES)

Despite declaring on Christmas day that work would resume the following day, Donald Trump was found golfing for four consecutive days. The former reality TV personality previously criticized Barack Obama for hitting the links, yet Trump is currently on pace to surpass the total number of golf outings his predecessor logged. 

Philip Bump posted on Twitter on December 29, 2017: "Updated my tracker of Trump s appearances at Trump properties. 71 rounds of golf including today s. At this pace, he ll pass Obama s first-term total by July 24 next year." Along with this was the link https://t.co/Fg7VacxRtJ and an image.

Given this backdrop, a discovery made by a Washington Post journalist regarding Trump's official website stands out as particularly strange, though much of this administration's behavior is unusual. Buried within the backend code was a direct mention of Obama and golf: "Unlike Obama, we are working to fix the problem and not on the golf course." 

However, the implementation of this code was flawed. Christopher Ingraham posted on Twitter on December 28, 2017: "The website of Donald Trump, who has spent several days in a row at the golf course, is coded to serve up the following message in the event of an internal server error: https://t.co/zrWpyMXRcz" with an accompanying image.

Ingraham added in subsequent tweets on December 28, 2017: "That snippet of code appears to be on all https://t.co/dkhw0AlHB4 pages, which the footer says is paid for by the RNC?" and "It s also all over https://t.co/ayBlGmk65Z. As others have noted in this thread, this is weird code and it s not clear it would ever actually display, but who knows."

Shortly after the hidden text was exposed publicly, the mention of Obama was purged from the site. Christopher Ingraham provided an update on December 29, 2017: "UPDATE: The golf error message has been removed from the Trump and GOP websites. They also fixed the javascript  =  vs  ==  problem. Still not clear when these messages would actually display, since the actual 404 (and presumably 500) page displays a different message" alongside an image.

Ingraham further noted on December 29, 2017: "That suggests someone at either RNC or the Trump admin is sensitive enough to Trump s golf problem to make this issue go away quickly once people noticed. You have no idea how much I d love to see the email exchange that led us here."

Furthermore, the programming itself was botched. A user going by the handle @tw1trsux pointed out on December 28, 2017: "The code was f-cked up. The best part about this is that they are using the  =  (assignment) operator which means that bit of code will never get run. If you look a few lines up  errorCode  will always be  404". Tim Peterson echoed this sentiment on the same day, tweeting, "trump s coders can t code. Nobody is surprised."

Ultimately, Donald Trump's preoccupation with Obama manifested even within the technical backend of his web presence while he continued his repeated visits to the golf course. Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images.

subject: worldnews
text:
BERLIN (Reuters) - German Chancellor Angela Merkel struck an optimistic note on Friday regarding the prospects of forming a government with the Greens and the pro-business Free Democrats (FDP), though her prospective allies warned that negotiations could still break down. Following an election last month that saw her bloc lose support to the far right—and with the Social Democrats (SPD), her previous coalition partners, insisting on moving to the opposition—Merkel is forced to unite three very different political factions to achieve a majority. Ahead of a Monday evening meeting between party chiefs and subsequent detailed discussions by larger teams, Merkel acknowledged to reporters that challenging negotiations are ahead, while maintaining that a successful agreement is possible through hard work and effort.

Should the coalition talks collapse, the likely outcome would be fresh elections, which could provide further momentum to the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) after their parliamentary breakthrough last month. Martin Schulz, the leader of the SPD, dismissed any possibility of reviving the outgoing "grand coalition" if Merkel's current efforts fall through. Speaking to the RND newspaper chain for an interview scheduled for Saturday publication, Schulz stated that a failure by Merkel to form a government would necessitate new elections. Similarly, FDP parliamentary group leader and negotiator Marco Buschmann told the Saturday edition of Die Welt that his party was prepared to transition to the opposition if the alliance did not materialize. Buschmann noted that while a new election might bolster the AfD—which entered parliament with 13 percent of the vote—voters might not use the party as a vehicle for protest if the distinctions among the remaining parties were more apparent.

Negotiators reported that Friday's discussions yielded agreement on easing the financial strain on families, expanding child care availability, and fighting child poverty. Furthermore, the potential partners aligned on backing Germany's commitments to NATO and other international organizations, deepening ties with France, and preserving positive relations with Russia. Nevertheless, significant disagreements persist over topics such as immigration limits, timelines for phasing out coal, climate change strategies, and rising defense expenditures. Additionally, the contentious topic of transportation was entirely bypassed on Friday. FDP deputy leader Wolfgang Kubicki shared with reporters that participants resolved to treat one another more kindly, noting his willingness to give it a try provided everyone cooperates.

Over the weekend, the parties are set to refine their core agendas prior to Monday's leadership summit led by Merkel. Michael Kellner, a prominent negotiator for the Greens, remarked that all the necessary components are present and must now be blended into a cohesive outcome. Conversely, fellow Green negotiator Juergen Trittin adopted a harsher stance in an interview with ARD television, pointing out that after 10 days and 12 discussed topics, the participants have not even managed to agree on their points of disagreement. Both FDP chief Christian Lindner and Buschmann estimated the likelihood of a successful coalition at fifty-fifty, while Green foreign policy specialist Omid Nouripour suggested the discussions could break down entirely. 

While Merkel has expressed her anticipation of a stable administration prior to Christmas, top conservative allies suggest the process might extend into the coming year. Horst Seehofer, the embattled leader of the CSU—the Bavarian sister party to Merkel's CDU—expressed encouragement over what he described as constructive and reliable talks among party leaders lately, while calling on negotiators to keep their disputes private. Advocating for a fresh start in the upcoming days, Seehofer faced criticism from his party's youth wing after pulling out of a scheduled speech to the group, which has advocated for a more contemporary appeal ahead of next year's Bavarian regional elections. Hans Reichhart, who leads the CSU youth organization, warned that this cancellation might worsen discussions surrounding Seehofer's political future following the steep losses sustained in the September 24 election. Prior to this, Seehofer had asked members to postpone any leadership discussions until later in the month, claiming that such debate could weaken his standing during the coalition negotiations.

text:
SYDNEY (Reuters) - A friend of a British documentarian who was reported missing during a quest to locate an isolated tribe in Papua New Guinea reported on Thursday that the explorer has been seen near an airstrip and is waiting to be flown out. Benedict Allen set out in the preceding month to find the Yaifo, an untamed community situated in the northern territory of the isolated South Pacific nation. He traveled without any communication devices and failed to establish an itinerary or an extraction strategy, as explained to Reuters by his associate, Frank Gardner. 

Allen had previously indicated on his blog that his return to the UK was scheduled for the middle of November. Prior to his departure, he posted a message on Twitter on October 11 telling people not to attempt a rescue and noting that nobody would be able to locate him in that part of PNG. However, concern grew among his relatives and associates when he failed to board his scheduled flight home the previous weekend. 

Gardner, who works as the security correspondent for the BBC, explained to Reuters that Allen remains in a vulnerable position. He is currently stranded in an isolated region of the country that can solely be accessed via aircraft because local tribal conflicts have resulted in the destruction of all road bridges. Preparations are presently moving quickly to arrange an emergency flight out for him before the violence spreads to his location. 

Before this update, Gardner informed the BBC that a local tribal commission had actively been searching for Allen, leading to his observation near an airstrip, though Reuters could not independently verify this report. On his personal website, Allen identifies as an adventurer and recounts past expeditions, including an earlier journey in PNG where he endured daily beatings for a period of six weeks as part of an initiation ceremony. His previous travels also feature a trek through a secluded area of the Amazon rainforest where, suffering from severe malaria and starvation, he had to consume his dog.

subject: politicsNews
text:
MOSCOW — On Thursday, Moscow advised Washington to independently investigate the email hacking controversy surrounding the Democratic Party, while simultaneously dismissing Donald Trump’s remarks—which he later claimed were sarcastic—urging Russia to locate Hillary Clinton’s unreturned messages.

The Republican presidential nominee provoked outrage from Democrats a day earlier by publicly calling on Russia to track down tens of thousands of messages from Clinton's time leading the State Department. This followed statements from President Barack Obama suggesting Moscow might attempt to sway the upcoming November 8 election following a Democratic National Committee email leak that cybersecurity specialists attributed to Russian actors.

The Kremlin has firmly rejected any notion of Russian involvement, labeling the allegations as baseless and accusing American politicians of exploiting Cold War anxieties and inventing narratives for political gain. While President Vladimir Putin has attempted to maintain neutrality regarding the American candidates, he has also described the populist businessman as exceptionally gifted, and state-run Russian television broadcasts have generally favored Trump over Clinton.

Speaking on Thursday, Kremlin representative Dmitry Peskov characterized the claims of Russian interference in the Democratic email leaks as verging on absolute absurdity driven by Russophobia. He firmly brushed aside Trump’s remark regarding the retrieval of Clinton’s correspondence, stating that handling those document batches is not Moscow's concern, emphasizing a policy of non-interference and a dislike for foreign meddling in Russian domestic matters. Peskov added that Americans must resolve and understand the nature of these emails independently.

Trump, who has consistently stated his intention to improve bilateral ties with Moscow if elected, also drew criticism by suggesting he might weigh recognizing the Crimean peninsula as Russian territory following its 2014 annexation. Peskov noted that the Kremlin remained indifferent to this statement, asserting it would not alter their officially neutral position on the U.S. election. He remarked that politicians campaigning during a heated race frequently make bold statements that typically become more measured once they assume official responsibilities.

Addressing Trump's comments concerning Crimea, Ukraine's ambassador to the United Nations, Volodymyr Yelchenko, remarked on Thursday that Trump is not currently the American president. He added to reporters that established United Nations resolutions exist and expressed confidence that any future U.S. administration will respect those determinations. The 193-member UN General Assembly passed a resolution in March 2014 invalidating the Moscow-supported referendum that led to Crimea's secession from Ukraine.

Political observers note that a Trump victory would likely be well-received by the Kremlin, given the New York billionaire's frequent praise for Putin, his stated desire for peaceful relations with Russia, and his openness to forming a joint front with Moscow against the Islamic State. Furthermore, Trump's suggestion that he might reconsider NATO's collective defense commitment would likely be viewed favorably in Moscow, where the Western alliance is viewed as an obsolete relic of the Cold War.

NEW YORK (Reuters) - Digital publisher BuzzFeed has backed out of a Republican National Committee advertising agreement—which has been pegged at $1.3 million—due to concerns regarding the party’s presumptive presidential nominee, Donald Trump. 

Jonah Peretti, the chief executive officer and founder of BuzzFeed, explained the decision in a Monday message to the staff. He stated that the company refuses Trump advertisements for the identical reason they reject cigarette commercials: they pose a danger to well-being. Peretti elaborated in the memo, which was published on BuzzFeed.com, that the Trump presidential bid stands in direct opposition to the liberties enjoyed by staff members both domestically and globally. He pointed specifically to the proposed ban on international travel for Muslims, noting it would hinder employees from fulfilling their professional duties. 

Further statements were declined by BuzzFeed. While Politico placed the financial figure of the arrangement at $1.3 million, neither the RNC nor BuzzFeed would verify this specific amount. An official from the RNC, speaking on the condition of anonymity, explained that the agreement represented under 1 percent of the committee's roughly $150 million advertising allocation. Furthermore, the official characterized the arrangement merely as an ad space reservation rather than a binding guarantee to run advertisements on the platform. Hope Hicks, a spokesperson for the Trump campaign, stated she had no additional comments to offer.

The Republican National Committee serves as the governing body for the Republican Party on a national level. Donald Trump is anticipated to formally secure the party's nomination for the November 8 United States presidential election during the upcoming July convention.

text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) — According to the leading Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, the panel's chairman stepping away from his role on Thursday provides a clean slate for the ongoing investigation into Russian meddling in the American presidential election. text:
SYDNEY (Reuters) - A decisive majority of Australians have cast their ballots in favor of same-sex marriage, setting the stage for lawmakers to enact legislation before 2017 concludes and touching off jubilant, rainbow-hued festivities on Wednesday featuring participants in wedding attire and glittering outfits who proclaimed that their affection is genuine. Should parliament approve the measure—a step anticipated despite resistance from vocal conservative elements on the government's right flank—Australia will join the ranks of 26 countries that legally recognize these unions. 

As the nation's lead statistician broadcasted the outcome live on a large display in a Sydney park, showing that 61.6 percent of surveyed participants supported marriage equality while 38.4 percent opposed it, crowds of thousands erupted into cheers, embraced, and wept. 

Ian Thorpe, an Australian Olympic swimmer who publicly revealed his sexuality three years prior, described the outcome as a massive weight lifted. Speaking to journalists at the Sydney gathering, Thorpe stated that the outcome establishes equality for individual feelings toward another person, regardless of identity. 

Although the postal survey carried no legal obligation, Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull swiftly affirmed his commitment to introducing a parliamentary bill with the objective of securing passage by Christmas. Turnbull minimized fears of a fracture within his governing coalition, even as conservative members pushed for modifications to safeguard religious liberties that would permit discrimination against same-sex partners. 

Addressing journalists in Canberra following the release of the figures, Turnbull characterized the mandate as clear and massive, noting that millions had spoken and delivered an overwhelming endorsement of marriage equality, voting in favor of fairness, dedication, and affection. A formal marriage equality proposal was subsequently presented to parliament on Wednesday afternoon. 

This outcome represents a historic milestone for LGBTQ+ equality in the country, where homosexual acts remained a criminal offense in certain states until 1997. American television personality Ellen DeGeneres, whose spouse is Australian actress Portia de Rossi, posted a message celebrating the news with the phrase, "It's a g day. Way to go Australia." 

Participation reached nearly 80 percent of qualified voters, surpassing turnout levels seen during the UK Brexit vote and the Irish marriage equality referendum. Fifty-nine-year-old Mark Barry shed tears alongside Gerrard Boller, his partner of three decades and five years, remarking to Reuters that he knew a celebrant who would be thrilled by the outcome. 

Alan Joyce, the Irish-born CEO of Qantas Airways and one of Australia's prominent openly gay corporate executives, addressed the Sydney assembly—many shielding themselves beneath rainbow-patterned parasols—calling the outcome phenomenal and pressing Turnbull to expedite the legislative process. 

Having faced strain from a parliamentary citizenship crisis that stripped him of his deputy and his majority in the legislature, Turnbull found himself, according to political analysts, presented with his initial chance in months to demonstrate definitive authority through the resounding affirmative vote. Monash University political scientist Nick Economou noted that Turnbull should draw strength from the outcome, viewing it as the decisive leadership opportunity he had been seeking. 

Throughout the campaign, the opposing side had mobilized major religious institutions, a strategy that proponents of the measure condemned as harsh and polarizing. Sydney's Catholic Archbishop, Anthony Fisher, expressed profound disappointment that the anticipated outcome would lead to laws further dismantling the traditional structure of marriage and the family in Australia. Bolstered by the strength of the affirmative vote, however, conservative politicians abandoned a rival proposal that would have permitted commercial enterprises, such as bakeries, to deny services like wedding cakes to same-sex couples based on religious objections.

Speaking alongside French leader Francois Hollande at the Kremlin on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed that Moscow had previously shared the schedule and route of the downed aircraft with the United States. Asserting that the U.S. heads the coalition of which Turkey is a member, Putin stated that the American side was fully aware of the timing and coordinates of their flights, which led to them being struck precisely at that location and moment. Furthermore, Putin alleged that the U.S. passed along this insider knowledge directly to the Turkish government.

Prior to his discussions with Hollande, Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan exchanged sharp rhetoric, with the Russian head of state demanding an apology that Erdogan flatly refused to offer. Defending the military action near the Syrian frontier, Erdogan insisted that Turkey's sovereignty and border protection measures must be acknowledged following the downing of the Russian jet over claimed airspace violations.

Rejecting Ankara's assertion that they would have held fire had they recognized the jet's Russian nationality, Putin labeled the defense as complete nonsense. Pointing out that their aircraft bear clear and easily recognizable identification markings, Putin expressed frustration that rather than guaranteeing such an incident never recurs, they are met with vague justifications and a refusal to apologize.

Additionally, Putin leveled accusations against Turkey regarding the purchase of petroleum from the Islamic State militant group, which depends heavily on energy sales for financial support. Insisting there is zero question that petroleum originating from terrorist-held parts of Syria is crossing the border into Turkish territory, Putin noted that aerial surveillance tracks these tanker trucks moving toward Turkey around the clock. He further characterized these shipments as carrying the blood of Russian citizens, explaining that extremists use the generated funds to acquire weaponry and munitions to carry out violent attacks.

text:
According to individuals familiar with the matter, a probe led by Republican Representative Devin Nunes aimed at determining whether the Obama administration improperly utilized classified intelligence to undermine Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign could ultimately harm both the congressman and the sitting president. 

Insiders note that the documents in question lack any proof that aides to former Democratic President Barack Obama engaged in misconduct. Instead, the material suggests that certain individuals associated with Trump may have breached the Logan Act, a little-known 18th-century statute from 1799 that bars private American citizens from engaging in unauthorized negotiations with foreign governments involved in disputes with the U.S. 

Furthermore, these intelligence reports intersect with the ongoing probe led by special counsel Robert Mueller regarding U.S. intelligence conclusions that Moscow interfered in the November election to support Trump, according to sources who requested anonymity. Mueller's office chose not to issue a statement. The Russian government, which faces American sanctions over human rights violations and the 2014 annexation of Crimea, has consistently rejected accusations of electoral interference. Meanwhile, Trump has repeatedly denied any collusion between his campaign team and Moscow, a controversy that has cast a shadow over his administration.

Nunes, who heads the House Intelligence Committee and maintains a close alignment with Trump, held a clandestine meeting earlier in the year with a White House intelligence staffer before alleging that Obama's team had requested the identities of American citizens appearing in intercepted communications involving Russians and other foreign nationals. The White House declined to provide comments when approached. 

While such names are typically redacted from intelligence intercepts, Nunes claimed that Obama's staff leaked the identities to sabotage Trump's presidential run. A representative for Samantha Power, the former U.N. ambassador whom Republicans and Nunes targeted over allegations of seeking political ammunition, stated that her review of intelligence reports was strictly limited to her official responsibilities. Conversely, a spokesperson for former national security adviser Susan Rice—another official accused by Republicans of mishandling intelligence—did not reply to inquiries.

Special counsel Mueller is actively probing encounters and discussions involving foreign officials, foreign business figures, and Trump associates. Those figures include the president's son-in-law and adviser Jared Kushner, eldest son Donald Trump Jr., former campaign chairman Paul Manafort, and former national security adviser Michael Flynn. 

“An obvious question is how all these meetings and conversations were set up,” one source remarked. “Who set them up? What was their purpose? What were the agendas? Who approved them? Who was briefed on them afterward? Signals intelligence might shed some light on that.” Representatives for the various Trump associates did not respond to requests for comment.

Meanwhile, Democrats argue that the claims regarding leaks brought forward by Nunes and other Republicans are a strategic effort to divert attention away from the multiple congressional inquiries and Mueller's investigation into Russia. 

While the National Security Agency routinely conceals the names of American citizens within intercepted communications, individuals holding the appropriate security clearances have the authority to request unmasked identities for legitimate intelligence reasons. 

“Unmasking Americans is extremely sensitive, and unmasking political opponents is really problematic,” a congressional official noted on condition of anonymity, adding that any requests by Obama administration personnel that lacked proper justification would merit an investigation. However, when pressed for concrete proof that Power or other former aides leveraged intelligence for political gain or leaked it to the press, the official declined to comment.

subject: worldnews
text: According to El Pais, the Spanish state prosecutor requested on Thursday that the Supreme Court place the speaker of the Catalan parliament and three other legislators behind bars while an investigation proceeds regarding their involvement in the region's unauthorized independence movement. Carmen Forcadell, who leads the Catalan parliament, along with five regional politicians, appeared in court on Thursday to face accusations including rebellion, sedition, and the improper use of public funds. The publication also noted that the prosecutor recommended freeing two additional regional lawmakers, though details regarding any potential conditions for their release were not specified.

subject: worldnews
text:
SOFIA (Reuters) — According to the interior ministry, a tragic collision on a central Bulgarian highway on Friday left nine individuals dead and 19 more hurt after a minibus plowed into a truck. The fatalities included the driver of the bus, which was transporting visually impaired passengers home following a trip to Dryanovo. Several of the survivors sustained critical injuries. 

Taking place shortly after midday (1000 GMT), the crash happened near the village of Mikre—situated roughly 130 kilometers (81 miles) west of Sofia—along the highway linking the nation's capital to the Black Sea port of Varna. Hospitalization was provided to the wounded, though the ministry did not specify the exact count of those listed in critical condition. 

While the precise triggers of the crash remain undetermined, the interior ministry noted that Prime Minister Boyko Borissov directed the transport ministry to conduct a thorough examination of the minibus. Meanwhile, reports from domestic media outlets indicated that the specific segment of roadway near Mikre has been the site of at least eight major automobile accidents resulting in 10 fatalities since 2014. 

Bulgaria, home to 7.1 million residents, maintains the highest rate of traffic fatalities within the European Union. Figures released by the interior ministry indicate that 535 people lost their lives in roadway accidents across the country during the first ten months of 2017.

subject: News
text:
Donald Trump renewed his attacks on Megyn Kelly via Twitter following her refusal to be won over by him. In a recent Vanity Fair interview, the Fox News anchor detailed how Trump sought to curry favor with her prior to launching his presidential campaign last summer, noting that she was impervious to his efforts. She recounted receiving press clippings about herself bearing his signature, alongside occasional phone calls praising specific segments. She added that his motives became apparent once his candidacy was announced, emphasizing that she remained neutral toward him and unswayed by his overtures. 

Kelly's firm stance against Trump was previously highlighted during an August debate where she pressed him hard. That confrontation prompted a sharp retort from Trump, who suggested she was bleeding from her eyes, and the hostility persisted even during her vacation, fueled by his conservative supporters. 

Reacting to her recent statements in Vanity Fair, Trump took to Twitter to insult her appearance and dismiss her appeal. He wrote that Kelly claimed she could not be wooed by him, adding that she was entirely average and questioning who would want to woo her. This post was shared on January 11, 2016. Kelly has been married twice, demonstrating that other men have successfully won her affection despite Trump's lack of success.

subject: politicsNews
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Anthony Scaramucci is stepping down from his position as White House communications director, just over a week after President Donald Trump appointed him to the role, according to an announcement from the administration on Monday. The departure follows a vulgar public outburst directed at fellow senior West Wing officials by Scaramucci last week, and it coincides with the swearing-in of John Kelly as the new chief of staff tasked with imposing order on the administration. In an official statement, the White House explained that Scaramucci believed stepping aside was the proper way to provide Kelly with a fresh start and the freedom to assemble his own staff.

subject: worldnews
text:
JAKARTA (Reuters) - Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency reported that 40,000 individuals have been cleared out from the vicinity of Bali's active Mount Agung volcano, though a significant portion of the population still needs to relocate following a Monday warning regarding a potential major blast. 

Sutopo, representing the disaster mitigation agency BNPB, emphasized the urgency during a press briefing, stating that immediate evacuation is crucial for everyone within the hazardous area due to the threat of a more severe explosion.

BRUSSELS/MADRID — Carles Puigdemont, the removed leader of Catalonia, announced on Tuesday that he would participate in the upcoming regional snap vote called by Madrid after the central authorities seized control of the area to halt its secession bid. Nevertheless, he insisted that the campaign for independence would persist. 

Meanwhile, Spain's High Court summoned Puigdemont alongside thirteen members of his dismissed cabinet to appear in Madrid for hearings on Thursday and Friday. During these proceedings, the court will advance allegations of breach of trust, sedition, and rebellion against the group. Following the Spanish legal framework, a magistrate will determine whether the politicians ought to be detained while a thorough probe and potential trial are prepared. 

Puigdemont relocated to Brussels following the regional parliament's unilateral declaration of secession on Friday, leaving uncertainty over whether he would comply with the Madrid tribunal's order. Belga news agency reported that the Belgian crisis unit was reviewing whether local authorities needed to provide security for Puigdemont during his stay. Earlier on Tuesday, he stated that he would only travel back to Spain if the government offered unspecified assurances. 

The agreement by Puigdemont to contest the December 21 regional ballot indicated that, for the moment, the administration in Madrid has secured the upper hand in the prolonged confrontation regarding the prosperous northeastern region, which previously held substantial autonomy. Resistance to the central government's enforcement of direct rule failed to materialize at the beginning of the week, leaving the separatist leadership disorganized. However, a survey published on Tuesday revealed that backing for a separate Catalan state reached its highest point in nearly three years during October. 

Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy had moved to dismiss the regional assembly less than an hour after the declaration was issued on Tuesday, while Spain’s Constitutional Court simultaneously blocked the measure in a largely symbolic action that gained no traction. 

Addressing a press conference in Brussels after dropping out of public view over the weekend, Puigdemont urged the Catalan populace to brace for a lengthy endeavor, asserting that democracy would form the basis of their triumph. He also clarified that he was not seeking asylum in Belgium. 

Rajoy, who has maintained an inflexible position throughout the standoff, is wagering that anti-secession factions will capture the regional legislature and halt the independence movement. Conversely, Puigdemont banks on robust support for the pro-independence faction to revitalize the secessionist movement following several turbulent weeks. 

The Spanish administration reiterated over the weekend that Puigdemont was welcome to run in the election, though it maintained that the judicial proceedings were an entirely separate concern. On Tuesday, the Supreme Court likewise initiated the processing of rebellion and sedition charges targeting regional parliament speaker Carme Forcadell and other prominent leaders. 

Triggered by an October 1 independence referendum, the political crisis stands as Spain's most severe since the restoration of democracy in the late 1970s. Although Spanish courts deemed the vote illegal and less than half of eligible citizens participated, the pro-secession regional government argued the outcome granted a mandate for statehood. Governments in the United States, France, Germany, and Britain have all thrown their weight behind Rajoy while dismissing the prospect of an independent Catalan nation, though certain capitals have urged both sides to engage in dialogue. 

Previously, Puigdemont, Vice President Oriol Junqueras, and other regional figures maintained they would refuse their removal from office. Yet their respective political organizations, Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya and PdeCat, announced on Monday that they would enter the vote, signaling tacit compliance with direct administration from Madrid. 

While separatist sentiment endures in the Basque Country and other regions, the current struggle has fractured Catalonia internally and provoked deep resentment across the rest of Spain. Although two recent surveys hinted that pro-independence momentum might be declining, an official regional poll released Tuesday indicated that roughly 48.7 percent of Catalans favor independence, climbing from 41.1 percent in June and marking the peak since December 2014. The Centre d'Estudis d'Opinio survey, based on 1,338 interviews conducted mostly between October 16 and October 29, represented the initial poll published following the independence declaration. 

Despite his journey to the heart of the European Union, Puigdemont's aspirations to draw the bloc into his dispute appear unlikely to succeed. Member nations have reaffirmed their commitment to Spanish unity, while EU officials in Brussels emphasize that they will interact solely with Madrid, treating the conflict as a strictly internal matter. Mina Andreeva, a European Commission spokesperson, stated in Brussels on Tuesday that their stance remains unchanged. 

Even so, certain analysts argue that the conflict will not dissipate swiftly. Raj Badiani, an economist with IHS Markit in London, noted that Spain faces an era of disruption, with its policy focus consumed by a single political debate while other major challenges are sidelined, drawing parallels to the UK and Brexit. Badiani added that more tangible economic fallout could emerge by early 2018 as uncertainty mounts with Catalans pressing harder for a legally binding referendum. 

Prominent Catalan business associations have endorsed direct rule and urged corporations to maintain their operations locally. Nevertheless, the crisis has already driven over 1,000 companies to relocate their legal bases away from Catalonia, a territory generating roughly a fifth of the economy in Spain, which ranks as the fourth-largest in the euro zone. Spain's IBEX index dipped slightly as Puigdemont began his Brussels address before recovering. 

For some residents in Barcelona, exhaustion appears to be the dominant sentiment. Ernesto Hernandez Busto, a 42-year-old editor, described the situation as farcical and entirely ridiculous, stating that extreme nationalism and separatism have plunged Catalonia into the most absurd predicament and worst inconvenience experienced over the past forty years.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Speaking in Columbus, Ohio, on Tuesday, Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton warned that a victory by her Republican opponent, Donald Trump, would trigger what she termed a "Trump recession" and spell ruin for the American economy. Clinton emphasized that her warning transcended standard partisan disputes, pointing out that economists across the political spectrum—left, right, and center—share the view that Trump's economic policies would trigger a new downturn.

This address in Ohio, a crucial battleground state for the November 8 election, marked Clinton's second major speech arguing that the wealthy real estate developer lacks the temperament required for the presidency. Her previous address focused on national security and foreign policy. 

Focusing on Trump's core argument for his candidacy, Clinton remarked, “Donald Trump has said he is qualified to be president because of his business record. So let’s take a look at what he did for his businesses: He’s written a lot of books about business. They all seem to end at Chapter 11; go figure.” The remark was a pointed reference to corporate bankruptcy filings under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.

The former secretary of state went on to characterize Trump as a self-described "king of debt," accusing him of running up massive liabilities that ultimately forced his enterprises into bankruptcy, costing numerous employees their jobs and destroying value for shareholders. She cautioned that applying such an approach to the federal government would terrify investors and potentially spark an economic disaster.

Simultaneously, Trump took to Twitter during the speech to respond: “I am ‘the king of debt.’ That has been great for me as a businessman, but is bad for the country. I made a fortune off of debt, will fix U.S.”

Clinton additionally targeted the presumptive Republican nominee's tax proposal, which seeks to streamline the tax code and cut the maximum corporate tax rate from 35 percent down to 15 percent, arguing it favors the rich at the expense of working-class households. She noted that according to projections by the nonpartisan Tax Foundation, the proposal would expand the federal deficit by $9.5 trillion over the coming ten years.

Addressing international commerce, Clinton argued that Trump's proposal to abandon existing trade accords could ignite trade wars, asserting that these pacts should instead be revised if they fail to serve American workers properly. She also maintained that Trump's proposals to construct a wall on the southern border and deport undocumented residents would destabilize the labor force and prove catastrophic for the U.S. economy.

The economic clash unfolded as both campaigns geared up for an intense electoral battle, with Trump scheduled to deliver an address countering Clinton in New York on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Trump's campaign operation deployed an increased volume of rapid-response emails during Tuesday's speech, arguing that Clinton's immigration platform would depress wages and pointing out that her husband, former President Bill Clinton, had previously supported unfavorable trade agreements.
